d: Magnus Carlsen didn't make a move. He didn't even sit at the board. Yet his decision to forfeit against Bibisara Assaubayeva has become one of the biggest talking points in chess. At the Total Chess event in Budapest, Carlsen had already sealed the match before the Fast Classical game, but chose not to play. Rupha Ramani looks at the chess format, the forfeit, the rating implications, FIDE's response and whether the rules allowed Carlsen to walk away without paying a sporting price.
